claim_being_audited: That certifying the model for launch is policy-compliant and evidentially supported despite the unresolved energy outage response performance gap, based on aggregate readiness, model-card documentation, and post-launch monitoring.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence satisfies the policy threshold.
A weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case.
Product labels such as non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality when the affected segment is named in customer commitments or legal review is pending.
Material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Public governance guidance can support documentation and monitoring, but it cannot substitute for the specific internal policy requirement above.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the energy outage response gap must be disclosed for launch.
Approved risk acceptance covering this specific named-use-case limitation, if one exists.
The actual model-card or launch disclosure showing the material limitation was disclosed before launch.
Evidence that the energy outage response segment gap was remediated to target before certification.
specific_concerns: The failing segment is named in two utility pilot commitments, which makes the weakness material under the stated policy.
The release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
There is admissible evidence of an open legal review on whether disclosure is required, with no final answer.
No admissible evidence shows the gap was resolved before launch.
No admissible evidence shows an approved risk acceptance exists.
Public guidance about documenting limitations and monitoring risk does not by itself satisfy the release policy predicate for a material named-use-case weakness.
unsupported_claims: That aggregate readiness plus documentation/monitoring is sufficient to make certification policy-compliant for this case.
That the remaining issue can be managed post-launch instead of being disclosed without evidence of resolution or approved risk acceptance.
Any implication that product's non-core or low-volume framing defeats materiality for a named committed segment.
